body.statement: The endpoint-attainment theorem makes both minimizing sets defining \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) nonempty on \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\). Determine the exact asymptotic order of \(s_\star(m,r,k)\). For the upper direction, establish one uniform order bound that controls both \(s_L(o,e)\) and \(s_U(o,e)\) for every \((o,e)\in\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\). For the lower direction, construct compatible margin families for which \(\max\{s_L(o,e),s_U(o,e)\}\), with the two minima taken separately, has the matching order. In particular, decide whether the quadratic \(k^2\) term in \(N_\star\) is intrinsic or removable uniformly over \(\mathcal C_{m,r,k}\).
body.justification: The current polynomial support certificate is sufficient for computation but does not characterize the intrinsic complexity of exact causal witnesses.
body.gap: Xie--Li give fixed binary response tables and generic linear programming gives broad basic-feasible-solution bounds; neither provides a matched structured support frontier as alphabets grow.
body.consumer: A certificate standard for large categorical PoC audits needs the smallest worst-case witness format rather than a merely polynomial one.
